question: Should OpenClaw adopt this cross-product localization registry, readiness manifest, and release-gating architecture as a sponsored core initiative, and if so what independently landable order should the five dependent bundles follow?
rationale: The proposed work creates new shared runtime, protocol, and release-readiness ownership rather than repairing one established behavior; code review cannot choose the permanent core/product boundary or rollout order safely.

options.title: Sponsor and split the series
options.body: Approve a bounded architecture direction, remove the release-owned changelog edit, and ask for independently reviewable, proof-backed foundation slices in dependency order.

options.title: Keep it as RFC work
options.body: Leave the series draft while maintainers decide whether localization readiness belongs in core and which user-facing surfaces are in scope.

options.title: Prefer narrower fixes
options.body: Decline the shared architecture for now and direct contributors toward focused fixes for the existing localization reports.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and split the series
recommendation.body: Approve a bounded architecture direction, remove the release-owned changelog edit, and ask for independently reviewable, proof-backed foundation slices in dependency order.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the interconnected design and can clarify intended boundaries, while final sponsorship still requires a repository decision owner.
